deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a raw observation log, not a derivation. It records the oscillations of a magnetized needle read by mirror and scale, as in Gauss's magnetometer intensity work of 1832–1834. The previous page holds a similar series, and the next page begins the theory of a magnet acting at a distance. The heading 'Zweite Reihe. 12"87' means 'second series, assumed period T0 = 12.87 s'.

(1) Timing columns. Column 1 is the swing number n. Column 2 is the clock time t_n of the n-th passage (h m s). Only the changing parts are written: '5 2.54' means 3h5m2.54s, '54 10.36' means 3h54m10.36s, and so on. Column 3 is the reduced time r_n = t_n − n·T0, written as seconds after the minute 3h4m. Example: t_1 − 12.87 = 36.98 − 12.87 = 24.11. If the period were exactly 12.87 s, r_n would be constant. Its drift shows how the true period departs from T0.
- Block n = 0–5: r ≈ 23.88–24.15, mean ≈ 24.03.
- Block n = 231–240: r ≈ 24.46–24.52, mean ≈ 24.49.
- Block n = 506–511: r ≈ 23.87–24.03, mean ≈ 23.95.
These values allow a least-squares or mean-of-groups correction of T0. The period is slightly longer early on (r rises by about 0.46 s over about 235 swings, so T ≈ 12.872 s) and shorter later. This is consistent with larger arcs early in the series, and/or with changes in the field.

(2) Scale readings. Two pairs of numbers are written at n = 236 and n = 508.
- 646.575 and 650.487 are most plausibly the equilibrium (middle) scale positions.
- 940.15 and 401.525 are the swing arcs (amplitudes) in scale divisions.

(3) Logarithmic decrement. 'Decr. log. 0.00136' is the common-log decrement of amplitude per oscillation:
λ = [log10(940.15) − log10(401.525)] / (508 − 236) = 0.36949 / 272 = 0.0013584 ≈ 0.00136. (Check is mine; it agrees.)
This λ would be used to reduce the observed period to infinitely small arcs, and to describe the damping.
errors: Rows 506–511: recomputing t_n − 12.87·n (seconds after 3h4m) gives 23.78, 23.77, 23.70, 23.67, 23.76, 23.83. Gauss writes 23.98, 23.97, 23.90, 23.87, 23.96, 24.03, a uniform excess of 0.20 s. This is probably a slip in 506×12.87 (6512.02 used instead of 6512.22), or an unstated correction.

Rows 231–233: recomputation gives 24.51, 24.52, 24.55, against the written 24.47, 24.46, 24.49. Rows 234–240 agree exactly. Either the times or the residuals in these three rows contain small copying or arithmetic slips (about 0.04–0.06 s).
Rows 0–5 and 234–240 check exactly. The decrement 0.00136 is correct from the two amplitudes on the page (0.0013584).

results.what: Reduction of oscillation transit times by subtracting n times an assumed period, to detect period drift
results.modern_name: Method of coincidences / reduced transit times for period determination (O−C residuals)

results.what: Logarithmic decrement from amplitudes at two swing numbers: (log a1 − log a2)/(n2 − n1)
results.modern_name: Logarithmic decrement of a damped oscillator
results.usually_credited_to: Used by Gauss and Weber in magnetometer work (1830s)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine observational data reduction from Gauss's well-documented magnetometer oscillation experiments (period and log decrement). Nothing beyond known practice appears.

checkable.asserts: Evaluates to 23.78, versus the written 23.98 (0.20 offset)

transcription_corrections: Swing number '506' is written over another numeral (possibly '510' or '500'); the intended reading 506 is confirmed by the sequence 507–511.
